name: FortiGate — Internal Host Communicating with a High-Risk/Sanctioned Country
description:
Attacker objective
Command-and-control or data movement to infrastructure hosted in a high-risk or sanctioned jurisdiction.

Attack logic
Outbound banking traffic is normally to a stable set of business and cloud regions. The first time an internal host communicates with a high-risk or sanctioned country is a sanctions and threat concern.

Why this detection works
A new-terms model over (source host, destination country) auto-baselines normal destinations and fires on a new high-risk pairing.

False positives
A legitimate service hosted in-region.

Tuning
Allowlist verified destinations; review the destination ASN/service.

Required telemetry
FortiGate traffic logs (srccountry, dstcountry, source.ip).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. source.ip + dstcountry + destination ASN/IP: confirm business justification.
2. Any C2 or exfiltration to a sanctioned geography is high priority.
query: fortinet.firewall.srccountry:"Reserved" and fortinet.firewall.action:"accept" and fortinet.firewall.dstcountry:("Iran" or "Russian Federation" or "Russia" or "North Korea" or "Syria" or "Belarus" or "Cuba")
